options.text: The email for one repository only
The email recorded in your commits across all your repositories
The email of the repository's owner on the server

questions.explanation: The --global scope applies to your user account across every repository, and user.email is stamped onto the commits you make. A single repo can override it with a --local value.

questions.prompt: The same setting is defined at both the global and local levels. Which value does Git use?

options.text: The global value — it is broader
The local value — the most specific level wins
Git reports an error and uses neither

questions.explanation: Precedence runs system < global < local, so the most specific level in effect wins. A local (per-repository) value overrides a global (per-user) one.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Git configuration are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Local config is stored in the repository's .git/config file
The --global level applies to your user account
Git config files are written in INI format
You must reinstall Git to change a setting

questions.explanation: Local settings live in .git/config, global settings apply to your user, and the files are INI-formatted. Settings are changed any time with git config — no reinstall needed.

questions.prompt: To list every setting along with the file it came from, run: git config --list --______
questions.explanation: git config --list --show-origin prints each effective setting prefixed with the config file it originated from — the fastest way to debug a surprising value.

questions.prompt: Your pushed commits show a generic avatar and aren't linked to your GitHub profile. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: You used HTTPS instead of SSH
Your commit user.email doesn't match an email verified on your GitHub account
You forgot to run git init

questions.explanation: GitHub links commits to accounts by the commit's email address. If user.email doesn't match a verified email on your account, the commits won't be attributed to your profile.

questions.prompt: Match each config scope or command to what it does.

pairs.right: Applies to every user on the machine
Applies to your user account, all repos

questions.explanation: System is machine-wide, global is per-user, local is per-repository, and git config --list prints the settings currently in effect.
